lcvn.title: Language-Conditioned World Modeling for Visual Navigation
lcvn.authors: Yifei Dong; Fengyi Wu; Yilong Dai; Lingdong Kong; Guangyu Chen; Yetong Sha; Qiyu Hu; Feng Liu; Siyu Huang; Qi Dai; Zhi-Qi Cheng
lcvn.venue: arXiv2603.26741v2, 30 September 2026; no conference status verified
lcvn.problem: Offline real-robot trajectory prediction from one initial RGB frame and language. Despite navigation terminology, the model receives no corrective real observation during the predicted trajectory. Dataset 39,016 trajectories/117,048 instructions spans five robot sources; TartanDrive is held out for unseen evaluation.
lcvn.mechanism: Sections 3–4: data normalize displacement by dataset step size, filter backward/short trajectories and use Qwen 3.5-9 B assisted human-verified concise/intricate/landmark instructions. Paradigm 1 trains language-conditioned diffusion world model (LDiT) on 32×32 VAE latents; CLIP text cross-attention and action/time AdaLN condition next-state prediction, with independent frame noise levels (diffusion forcing,Eq. 2). A CVAE plan encoder aligns full-trajectory expert plans with current-state/instruction learner plans using KL (Eq. 3). Frozen world-model rollouts supervise actor–critic with intrinsic reward dot (expert, predicted)/max (norms)^2(Eq. 5), critic lambda-return MSE (Eq. 7), actor negative return plus plan KL/language alignment (Eq. 8). Paradigm 2 fine-tunes Anole 7 B to predict next action bins and visual tokens jointly (Eq. 11), feeding predicted views back autoregressively. It is not a closed-loop physical policy benchmark. Four A10080 GB GPUs; token context 4096 forces image resolution/context tradeoffs.
lcvn.novelty: Language-labeled heterogeneous robot benchmark and controlled comparison of separate latent imagination versus unified multimodal prediction. Adds language grounding beyond NWM, with actor–critic/latent-plan mechanisms inherited from prior control research.
lcvn.results: Table 1 p. 8 separate WM+AC unseen SR .19 versus unified 0.27, while seen 0.43 versus 0.42. Table 2 p. 9 separate model has better SSIM/LPIPS yet worse unseen navigation, directly separating fidelity from task utility. Table 4 p. 10 landmark instructions SR .47 for both, richer intricate .38/.40. Success is endpoint distance below robot average step size, not R2R three-meter success or collision-free execution.
lcvn.bottleneck: Open-loop trajectory errors compound without observation correction; intrinsic expert-latent similarity may penalize valid alternate routes. Model fidelity and navigation generalization diverge. The unified context/resolution tradeoff and different pretrained priors limit strict architecture-only conclusions.
lcvn.followups: Current frontier relative to NWM/Vid2World; WorldMAP and PiJEPA are further language-world-model leads. No reviewed evidence converts these offline scores into closed-loop safety or calibrated action risk.

learning_to_map.title: Learning to Map for Active Semantic Goal Navigation
learning_to_map.authors: Georgios Georgakis; Bernadette Bucher; Karl Schmeckpeper; Siddharth Singh; Kostas Daniilidis
learning_to_map.problem: ObjectNav with noiseless RGB-D and pose in unseen MP3D scenes. Predict semantic occupancy beyond the field of view and choose exploration goals using ensemble disagreement.
learning_to_map.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–7: project depth and semantic segmentation into 10 cm top-down cells. First UNet predicts occupancy over unknown/occupied/free channels; second takes predicted occupancy concatenated with projected semantics and outputs |C_s|×h×w class probabilities. Pixelwise CE trains both; semantic gradients flow through occupancy predictor. Four independently initialized predictors form an ensemble; mean is estimated semantic probability and variance is an epistemic proxy. After about 900 k initial examples, actively collect about 500 k examples maximizing average class variance (Eq. 1) and finetune. At deployment accumulate local maps by Bayes-style registration and select locations maximizing target mean + alpha×standard deviation (Eq. 2); compare lower-bound/mixed/mean variants. Frozen DD-PPO depth PointNav executes the chosen goal. Models do not update online during task evaluation.
learning_to_map.novelty: Separates active collection for map learning from uncertainty-guided target search; extends anticipated occupancy to semantic completion with an ensemble. UCB-style terminology is heuristic: the paper acknowledges unknown coverage probability, not a calibrated confidence theorem.
learning_to_map.results: Table 1 p. 7 active UCB SR 34.3±.9/SPL 13.3±.5 versus offline 30.1±.9/9.6±.4, BALD 30.4/9.6. Table 2 semantic IoU 25.6 versus offline 20.1. About 2480 episodes/11 target classes,56 train/11 val scenes; 500 steps, one-meter visible-object goal. Gains support collection strategy and map quality but not general calibration.
learning_to_map.bottleneck: Ground-truth pose/semantic training maps and four-model compute are strong requirements. Repeated correlated predictions registered as independent evidence can become overconfident. Variance can be low for shared bias; UCB scores have no stated finite-sample coverage guarantee.
learning_to_map.followups: SGM uses masked-map self-supervision and language priors; WMNav uses heuristic VLM curiosity. A proposal merely adding uncertainty-guided exploration or ensembles would overlap this work.

sgm.title: Imagine Before Go: Self-Supervised Generative Map for Object Goal Navigation
sgm.authors: Sixian Zhang; Xinyao Yu; Xinhang Song; Xiaohan Wang; Shuqiang Jiang
sgm.problem: ObjectNav from RGB-D, pose and an accumulated semantic map. Predict unobserved object/occupancy regions to select a long-term goal.
sgm.mechanism: Section 3: training global semantic maps are cropped/resized, patchified and randomly masked. ViT encodes visible patches f_v∈R^(n_v×d). Observed categories prompt an LLM for likely neighbors; frozen RoBERTa gives f_l∈R^(n_l×d). LXMERT-style cross-attention (Eq. 1) fuses geometry and language priors, and MAE decoder reconstructs masked multi-channel binary map patches. Loss is pixel BCE plus weighted object IoU (Eqs.2–3). At inference crop local map with enlarged bound (about 140%), resize 224, sample informative/frontier-adjacent patches using weighted normalized occupancy and Laplacian responses (Eq. 4). Predicted unknown cells are merged while observed cells override generated values. Target-channel argmax sets goal; low-confidence initial stages use exploration. Fast Marching replans local actions on occupancy. LLM responses are precomputed over category combinations; no online LLM call is necessary.
sgm.novelty: Self-supervised masked-map completion combines episode geometry and generic language relations, versus L2 M supervised local anticipation/ensembles. Self-supervised means no goal-action labels, not no map construction or pretrained segmentation requirements.
sgm.results: Table 2 p. 7 Gibson full SR 78.0/SPL 44.0, episodic-only 71.5/40.8, plus general knowledge 74.4/41.3; MP3D full 37.6/14.7 versus 31.9/12.2. Oracle target location Gibson 91.7/72.3 reveals substantial remaining localization/planning gap. Combined exploration and priors matter, not only decoder capacity.
sgm.bottleneck: Argmax predicted target can pursue hallucinated context; scores are confidence-like outputs without calibration evidence. Closed category combinations and semantic segmentation constrain open vocabulary. Resizing crops can distort metric precision; observed-value override helps provenance but does not validate unknown predictions.
sgm.followups: WMNav replaces learned map completion with VLM scores; WoMAP optimizes detector-derived latent rewards. Neither establishes that semantic prior maps recover correctly after confidently wrong predictions.

vid2world.title: Vid2World: Crafting Video Diffusion Models to Interactive World Models
vid2world.authors: Siqiao Huang; Jialong Wu; Qixing Zhou; Shangchen Miao; Mingsheng Long
vid2world.problem: Convert pretrained passive video generation into temporally causal, frame-level action-conditioned simulation for manipulation, games and visual navigation.
vid2world.mechanism: Sections 4.1–4.2: mask temporal attention and transform temporal convolution weights. Shift reuses weights at earlier indices; masked transfer discards future-facing weights; extrapolative transfer replaces future features by a local linear combination of past features and redistributes convolution weights. For a three-tap example z_(t+1)≈2 z_t−z_(t−1), effective weights become w_−1−w_1 and w_0+2 w_1. This preserves responses only under approximation assumptions. Diffusion forcing samples independent per-frame noise levels; action embeddings at time t use preceding action a_(t−1). Independent action dropout trains conditional/unconditional scores; guidance epsilon=(1+lambda) epsilon_cond−lambda epsilon_uncond. Theorem 4.1 interprets this as probability tilting toward action-consistent outcomes, not causal identification of unsupported interventions. DynamiCrafter 1.1 B initialization,100ksteps/about 7 days on 4 A100 forRT1. Inference autoregressively denoises latest frame with clean history.
vid2world.novelty: Systematic architecture and training adaptation of passive video priors, plus fine-grained action guidance. Distinct from training a navigation diffusion model from scratch or only adding a global action embedding.
vid2world.results: Table 1, p. 8: RT1 FVD is 18.5 versus 24.2 for the action-conditioned baseline. Some FID comparisons are flagged because baseline code did not set the Inception network to evaluation mode. On RECON, Vid2World FVD is 59.4 versus NWM 31.2, and LPIPS 0.3236 versus 0.295, although SSIM improves from 0.389 to 0.481. Thus there is no uniform dominance. Table 2, p. 9: extrapolative transfer plus guidance gives FVD 22.4 versus masked transfer plus guidance 25.8. The real-to-sim experiment ranks three RT1 drawer-policy checkpoints; this is a narrow validation setting.
vid2world.bottleneck: Guidance can overconcentrate probabilities and does not establish calibrated transition uncertainty. Local linear extrapolation fails under abrupt changes. Video metrics and a few policy-ranking examples do not demonstrate reliable VLN planning or all-action counterfactual validity.
vid2world.followups: NWM,LCVN and WorldVLN are navigation interfaces to compare. Proposed 'causal' world modeling must distinguish temporal masking, conditional guidance and actual intervention identification.

visualplanning.title: Visual Planning: Let's Think Only with Images
visualplanning.authors: Yi Xu; Chengzu Li; Han Zhou; Xingchen Wan; Caiqi Zhang; Anna Korhonen; Ivan Vulić
visualplanning.problem: Plan in fully visual grid environments (FrozenLake,Maze,MiniBehavior), outputting a sequence of images. This is not photorealistic, partially observed route-following.
visualplanning.mechanism: Section 2: LVM7 B autoregressively generates next visual states (Eq. 1). Warmup CE uses random-walk prefixes with a randomly sampled valid next-state target (Eq. 2), maintaining transition diversity. Stage 2 samples G next-image candidates and applies GRPO clipped importance ratios plus referenceKL (Eq. 3). A rule-based dynamics interpreter extracts whether the image transition is valid; a progress estimator classifies distance-decreasing, valid-nonprogressing or invalid moves, with rewards 1/0/−5(Eq. 4). Thus hidden symbolic environment knowledge supplies verification/reward even though model outputs are images. Inference generates a full visual plan; actions are implicit and parsed for evaluation.
visualplanning.novelty: Applies RL to image-sequence planning, comparing a visual-only pretrained backbone with textual multimodal reasoning. Not evidence that language is generally unhelpful; the benchmarks are deliberately vision-first and have exact verifiers.
visualplanning.results: Table 1, p. 6: VPRL averages EM 80.6/PR 84.9, versus visual SFT 56.1/65.2 and Qwen SFT 53.6/69.9. EM accepts any shortest valid trajectory by parsing environment states rather than requiring exact pixel equality. This comparison isolates the training change within LVM more clearly than it establishes modality superiority across differently pretrained backbones.
visualplanning.bottleneck: Rule-based interpreter and exact progress estimate are privileged; transferring to noisy unknown environments requires learned validators whose errors can be exploited. Warmup random targets encourage but do not prove full transition coverage. Synthetic grid success is not empirical navigation performance.
visualplanning.followups: FantasyVLN/CoT-VLA/WorldVLN use visual reasoning in richer embodied tasks but do not inherit exact grid verifiers. A new visual-planning proposal needs a reliable real-world outcome validator.

wmnav.title: WMNav: Integrating Vision-Language Models into World Models for Object Goal Navigation
wmnav.authors: Dujun Nie; Xianda Guo; Yiqun Duan; Ruijun Zhang; Long Chen
wmnav.problem: Training-free task-specific ObjectNav from panoramic RGB-D and pose. Pretrained VLMs provide semantic exploration scores and action choices, not a learned physical transition simulator.
wmnav.mechanism: Section III: rotate through six viewpoints, query PredictVLM for 0–10 directional target/exploration scores, project them into a metric curiosity map. Initialize unknown cells 10 and merge M_t=min (M_(t−1),M_nav_t)(Eq. 3). Project map scores back into views and select maximum average direction. PlanVLM uses previous subtask/current view to output next subtask and goal flag (Eq. 4). ReasonVLM selects annotated polar waypoint candidates. Exploration filters visited regions; goal-approaching mode removes length constraints and densely samples goal locations, then uses estimated distance for stop (Eq. 6). Three VLM roles are prompt configurations, without gradient updates. The 'cost' is subtask/flag prompt memory, not a learned reward model.
wmnav.novelty: Persistent curiosity map plus subtask memory and two-stage waypoint selection, extendingVLMNav-style annotated actions. Uses world-model terminology broadly for semantic prediction and memory; no action-conditioned next-RGB model is present.
wmnav.results: Table I, p. 6: HM3D v0.1 SR 58.1/SPL 31.2; MP3D 45.4/17.2. MP3D SPL is below VLFM 17.5 despite broad superiority wording. Table II, HM3D v0.2: adding the two-stage action proposal raises SR from 70.1 to 72.2 while reducing SPL from 34.7 to 33.3. Table III gives Qwen 3B SR 29.7 versus Gemini 1.5 Pro 58.1, showing substantial backbone dependence. HM3D versions must be compared separately.
wmnav.bottleneck: DEDUCTION: ordinary minimum merging prevents recovery from a falsely low exploration value when a later estimate rises. However, the released code explicitly resets identified goal-mask cells to 10, so this is a scoped limitation with a recovery exception. Prompt scores are not calibrated probabilities. The printed 1.0 versus 0.1 m stopping threshold is inconsistent, and the inspected code uses 0.8 m internally; exact configuration must be stated.
wmnav.followups: ImagineNav++ adds memory to visual imagination; SGM/L2 M supply learned map probabilities/uncertainty. Confidence recovery and observation-provenance are specific remaining concerns.

womap.title: WoMAP: World Models for Embodied Open-Vocabulary Object Localization
womap.authors: Tenny Yin; Zhiting Mei; Tao Sun; Lihan Zha; Miyu Yamane; Emily Zhou; Jeremy Bao; Ola Shorinwa; Anirudha Majumdar
womap.problem: Active 6 DoF camera localization of a language-specified object, maximizing visibility/detection reward. Primarily tabletop/robot active perception, not route instruction navigation.
womap.mechanism: Section 3: construct Gaussian Splat scenes from real video and sample arbitrary observation/pose pairs, deriving relative actions; no expert demonstrations required. Grounding DINO confidence×bounding-box size supplies dense target rewards. Frozen DINOv2 patch embeddings form z∈R^d; ViT dynamics predicts Gaussian next-latent parameters and a language-conditioned head predicts reward. Recurrent dynamics supervision is described as KL to true transition (Eq. 1), but empirical target distribution/variance must be checked in code. VLM chooses coarse textual action proposals; each is refined by differentiable MPC through latent dynamics, selecting highest predicted reward. Eq. 2 prints maximizing reward PLUS positive action-change L1 while calling it smoothness: the sign is inconsistent and requires source resolution. No pixel decoder is required.
womap.novelty: Combines real-to-sim data generation, detector-reward distillation and VLM-initialized latent action optimization. Closest DINO-WM predicts features; here explicit task rewards and proposal priors guide active perception.
womap.results: Figures 6–7 report 150 tasks/environment; Table 1 p. 8 hardware 20 trials per scene, WoMAP real 55/65/63% versus VLM 0/5/0. Table 2 nominal 63% falls to 50% under lighting and 30% under background shift, substantial residual sensitivity. Success is detector confidence/box-size threshold, potentially sharing reward bias; not object-goal navigation SR .
womap.bottleneck: Reward detector errors can be amplified by gradient optimization; predicted Gaussian spread is not shown calibrated. Object visibility differs from collision-free reachability. VLM proposals restrict explored modes; background shift halves success. The printed smoothing sign and exact dynamics likelihood need code audit.
womap.followups: DINO-WM,NWM,CVAML provide representation/planning/objective contrasts. A navigation proposal about model-basedVLM proposal refinement overlapsWoMAP strongly.
